paper_title: One Tokenizer To Rule Them All Emergent Language Plasticity via   Multilingual Tokenizers
caption: : Effect of vocabulary size.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the effect of vocabulary size on accuracy for two different tokenizers: "universal" and "cluster". The x-axis represents vocabulary size, labeled as "100k", "175k", and "250k", indicating a linear scale with values in thousands, and tick labels spaced at 75k intervals. The y-axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 40.5% to 42.0%, with major gridlines and tick labels at 0.5% intervals. The "universal" tokenizer is represented by a blue line with star markers, showing a steady increase in accuracy from 40.5% at 100k to 42.0% at 250k. The "cluster" tokenizer is represented by an orange line with circular markers, showing a slight decline in accuracy from 41.6% at 100k to 41.5% at 175k, and then a further decrease to 41.4% at 250k. The two lines cross between 175k and 250k, indicating that the "universal" tokenizer surpasses the "cluster" tokenizer in accuracy at larger vocabulary sizes.
